# Zillions repository guide for language models

Project: new browser-based science-fantasy MMO using Zillions as its current playable foundation
Production: https://zillions.taborlin.co
Repository: https://github.com/0xatd/zillions
Default branch: main

## Read first

- AGENTS.md: hard rules, workflow, and code map
- docs/product-contract.md: product boundaries and shipped behavior
- docs/architecture.md: modules, runtime flow, and state ownership
- docs/agent-brief.md: implementation details and known traps
- docs/backend.md: Supabase and Vercel data boundaries
- docs/review-guide.md: pull request review gate
- docs/art-direction.md: 3D shape language, scale, names, sockets, and budgets
- docs/art-pipeline.md: Blender source, GLB export, runtime fallback, and review
- docs/galaxy-meta-integration.md: how the galaxy and meta-progression modules wire into the shell

## Source of truth

1. Current source code and supabase/schema.sql
2. Automated checks in scripts/
3. docs/product-contract.md
4. docs/architecture.md
5. docs/agent-brief.md
6. Future design documents

## Runtime summary

- src/main.js composes the browser runtime.
- src/game.js owns deterministic simulation state.
- src/config.js owns balance, heroes, levels, plots, and items.
- src/terrain.js creates deterministic terrain and terrain-derived sites.
- src/map.js renders terrain relief and set dressing.
- src/overworld.js owns galaxy destinations, persistent world descriptors, Orbital Lifts, walking, and world-scoped ghost presence.
- src/overworld-parties.js owns overworld faction traffic: roads between settlements, party archetypes, and deterministic routing. main.js draws it.
- src/galaxy.js generates star systems, world kinds, threat tiers, and world descriptors from one seed.
- src/factions.js owns the faction roster, presence archetypes, and ownership assignment.
- src/crafting.js owns pure recipes, socket rules, component upgrades, and
  authority-ready mutation proposals.
- src/items.js owns item bases, weapons, affixes, damage types, and deterministic
  item generation. An item is a key; "base:seed:ilvl:rarity" resolves to a rolled
  item, a bare key resolves to an authored one.
- src/skilltree.js owns the Lattice, a 646-node shared passive tree generated
  from a fixed seed. Effects are data; rule-changing doctrines are flags read by
  src/game.js.
- src/keybinds.js owns the control scheme. Every action is declared once with a
  default key; main.js dispatches through it and Settings rebinds it. Keys are
  never literals in the input handler.
- src/lockstep-hash.js owns the per-window state hash peers compare. It is a pure
  function over a Game so it can be checked headless.
- src/meta.js owns run payouts, the meta-upgrade tree, and the run-start bonus payload.
- src/economy.js owns signed-in economy requests, legacy import, and snapshot projection.
- src/plots.js creates colony plans, ramparts, gates, and plots.
- src/lanes.js creates the deterministic lane graph.
- src/ui.js owns menus, lobby UI, HUD, and overlays.
- src/menu-vignette.js owns the menu attract show (presentation only, no sim).
- src/online.js owns Supabase room and signaling state.
- src/net.js owns WebRTC transport and diagnostics.
- src/auth.js owns sign-in, profiles, saves, and stats.
- src/supabase.js provides the one shared Supabase client.
- src/assets.js loads authored GLB assets and keeps procedural fallbacks.
- src/horde-art.js owns per-type instanced zombie models (presentation only).
- src/unit-art.js owns procedural troop and hero rigs (presentation only).
- src/building-art.js owns building meshes, walls and gates (presentation only).
- api/ contains Vercel server routes. api/economy.js is the authenticated,
  server-authoritative inventory and currency boundary.
- supabase/schema.sql is the database schema source.
- supabase/migrations/20260820203000_earth_region_topology.sql defines the
  dormant canonical universe, Earth region, faction-control, lease, and
  cross-region handoff authority.

## Critical rules

- Keep simulation deterministic.
- Do not use Math.random() in simulation code.
- Preserve snapshot and restore state.
- Do not restore day or night phases.
- Keep maps and colony plans terrain-derived.
- Use levelById() for level lookup.
- Keep the canonical seven-hero roster.
- Keep multiplayer version, connection, eligibility, Ready, and load gates.
- Never show private Google identity.
- Never commit secrets.
- Never seed fake production activity.
- Keep 3D presentation separate from deterministic collision and simulation.
- Validate authored GLBs and review silhouettes at gameplay distance.

## Validation

Run npm run check.
Run git diff --check.
Run a local Vercel production build.
Do not call a pull request deployable until all three pass.
